# pangram


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

[`pangram_text`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#pangram_text)
and
[`pangram_path`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#pangram_path)
send prose to [Pangram](https://www.pangram.com)’s AI-detection API
instead of running the rules. They read the same Markdown as
[`score_text`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/score.html#score_text)
and
[`score_path`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/score.html#score_path).
They return a
[`Result`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/score.html#result)
with the same addresses, JSON fields and `min_words` cutoff.
`slopometer --pangram` runs
[`pangram_path`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#pangram_path)
from the command line.

Pangram scores text in windows, which can run to hundreds of words. Each
finding is one window. Its weight is the window’s score multiplied by
10. A window that Pangram rates fully AI-written weighs 10, the same as
a kill-tier rule finding. The density is the mean window score, weighted
by word count, on a scale from 0 (human) to 100 (AI). Under `--pangram`,
`--threshold` compares against this scale.

Each request sends the text to Pangram’s servers and costs about $0.05
per 100 words. The functions read the API key from `PANGRAM_API_KEY`.

``` python
import json
from fastcore.test import *
from nbdev.config import get_config
```

## What Pangram reads

Pangram reads the blocks the rules read: headings, list items and
paragraphs, with code removed.
[`_pangram_input`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#_pangram_input)
joins them with single newlines and returns each block’s offset in the
joined text. Pangram collapses each blank line to one newline before it
reports window offsets. With single newlines, its offsets match the text
sent.

``` python
sd = get_config().config_path/'samples'
t2 = (sd/'theory2.md').read_text()
sent, offs = _pangram_input(segment(t2))
for b,o in zip(segment(t2), offs): test_eq(sent[o:o+len(b.txt)], b.txt)
sent[:200]
```

## Calling Pangram

Pangram runs each request as a task.
[`_predict`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#_predict)
posts the text to `/task`, then polls `/task/{id}` every half second
until the task’s `stage` is `STAGE_SUCCESS` or `STAGE_FAILED`. It
returns Pangram’s response as a dict. It raises an error when the task
fails or takes longer than `timeout` seconds.

`samples/theory2.pangram.json` holds Pangram’s response for
`samples/theory2.md`. The examples below read it, so they run without an
API key or network access. This cell recorded it:

``` python
(sd/'theory2.pangram.json').write_text(json.dumps(_predict(sent), indent=1))
```

``` python
payload = json.loads((sd/'theory2.pangram.json').read_text())
test_eq(payload['text'], sent)
{k: payload[k] for k in ('prediction_short', 'fraction_ai', 'fraction_ai_assisted', 'fraction_human')}, len(payload['windows'])
```

## Windows as findings

A
[`PangramFinding`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#pangramfinding)
is a
[`Finding`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/core.html#finding)
for one window. It adds Pangram’s score, label, confidence and word
count. Its display shows only the start of the window, because a window
can run to hundreds of words.

href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/pangram.py#L51"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### PangramFinding

``` python
def PangramFinding(
    start, # Character offset where the window starts
    end, # Character offset one past the window's end
    text, # The window's text
    score, # Pangram's `ai_assistance_score`, from 0 (human) to 1 (AI)
    label, # Pangram's label, such as 'AI-Generated' or 'Human Written'
    confidence, # 'High', 'Medium', or 'Low'
    words, # Words in the window
):
```

``` python
w = payload['windows'][0]
pf = PangramFinding(w['start_index'], w['end_index'], w['text'], w['ai_assistance_score'], w['label'], w['confidence'], w['word_count'])
test_eq(pf.weight, 10)
pf
```

[`PangramResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#pangramresult)
keeps Pangram’s response in `payload`. Its header shows the Pangram
score in place of the rules’ total weight.

``` python
    txt, # The scored document
    findings, # `PangramFinding`s, worst first
    words, # Word count across all scored blocks
    payload:NoneType=None, # Pangram's response; None when no request was sent
    min_words:int=150, # Minimum scored words; 0 disables the cutoff
):
```

### PangramResult.density

``` python
def density():
```

*Mean window score, weighted by word count and scaled to 0-100*

Density is the mean window score, weighted by word count and scaled to
0-100. A 300-word window scored 1.0 and a 100-word window scored 0.0
give a score of 75:

``` python
wins = [PangramFinding(0, 50, 'x'*50, 1.0, 'AI-Generated', 'High', 300), PangramFinding(50, 80, 'y'*30, 0.0, 'Human Written', 'High', 100)]
test_eq(PangramResult('x'*80, wins, 400, min_words=0).density, 75.0)
```

[`_pangram_result`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#_pangram_result)
maps each window’s offsets in the joined text back to the document. It
raises `ValueError` if Pangram’s text differs from the text sent.
Offsets into changed text would point at the wrong place. The recorded
response has one window, covering the whole sample:

``` python
r2 = _pangram_result(t2, payload, min_words=0)
f = r2.findings[0]
test_eq(t2[f.start:f.start+40], f.text[:40])
test_eq(t2[f.end-40:f.end], f.text[-40:])
r2
```


*Score markdown `txt` with Pangram, sending no request below `min_words`
scored words*

Below `min_words` scored words,
[`pangram_text`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/pangram.html#pangram_text)
returns a short result without sending a request:

``` python
short = pangram_text('robust widgets')
assert short.too_short
test_eq(short.density, None)
```
